answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is locked for the epoch and slashed if the identity is caught misbehaving. A newcomer starts with a whisper of trust, able only to observe, and must earn standing through verified work before it can transact at the summit of the market. Like a jade seal that is hard to forge and easy to check, the stake is cheap to verify but expensive to duplicate: an attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand stakes, so the cost of the attack grows linearly while the gain stays flat.
